gloss: phonology; sounds of a language; phoneme

definitions.gloss: phonology; sound system of a language
definitions.explanation: The study of or the system of distinctive sounds in a language. Used in linguistics to discuss how sounds function within a language.
An individual distinctive sound unit in a language. The smallest unit of sound that distinguishes meaning.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{音韻|おんいん}を{学|まな}ぶ。
{英語|えいご}と{日本語|にほんご}では{音韻|おんいん}{体系|たいけい}が{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: English and Japanese have very different phonological systems.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}{日本語|にほんご}の{音韻|おんいん}{体系|たいけい}は{現代|げんだい}とは{異|こと}なり、{母音|ぼいん}が8つあったとする{説|せつ}がある。
examples.english: The phonological system of ancient Japanese was different from the modern one, with a theory suggesting there were eight vowels.

examples.japanese: 「ん」は{一|ひと}つの{音韻|おんいん}だ。
{音韻|おんいん}の{違|ちが}いで{意味|いみ}が{変|か}わる。
examples.english: Differences in phonemes change the meaning.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}では「ら」と「la」の{音韻|おんいん}の{区別|くべつ}がないため、{英語|えいご}{学習者|がくしゅうしゃ}は{苦労|くろう}することがある。
examples.english: Since Japanese does not distinguish the phonemes "ra" and "la," learners of English sometimes struggle.

notes:
USAGE:
{音韻|おんいん} is a technical linguistics term composed of {音|おん} (sound) and {韻|いん} (rhyme, tone). It is commonly encountered in Japanese language study and linguistics courses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {音韻|おんいん}{体系|たいけい} (phonological system)
- {音韻|おんいん}{論|ろん} (phonology — the academic field)
- {音韻|おんいん}{変化|へんか} (sound change, phonological change)
- {音韻|おんいん}{規則|きそく} (phonological rules)

RELATED WORDS:
- {音声学|おんせいがく} (phonetics — the physical study of speech sounds)
- {音韻論|おんいんろん} (phonology — the abstract study of sound systems)
- {音素|おんそ} (phoneme — a more technical synonym for sense 2)
